wins: Enumerated exposed HTTP/SSH services and collected version banners within first 3 minutes (ep001_step03).
Captured weak HTTP auth mechanism enabling plan for credential stuffing (ep001_step07).
fails: Unable to deliver successful exploitation payloads; no system compromise achieved despite persistence attempts.
Mentor required intervention 10 times indicating recurring decision bottlenecks in lateral movement planning.
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance was effective and surfaced clear attack surfaces, but exploitation and persistence phases failed to progress, resulting in zero mission success.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Exploitation phase retries triggered by inability to bypass outdated payload filters, stalling rootcode delivery.

skill_cards.if_condition: When http service returns default login panel and content-type html
skill_cards.then_action: Run dirsearch with medium depth to identify hidden admin panels

skill_cards.if_condition: When SSH service banner reveals OpenSSH 7.x
skill_cards.then_action: Invoke nmap with ssh-brute and ssh2-enum-algos scripts for credential validation and key info

skill_cards.if_condition: When HTTP basic auth challenge observed
skill_cards.then_action: Use hydra with user list from recon and default password set to test credentials quickly

memory_ops.reason: Consistent recon wins identifying admin paths to focus exploitation.
SSH enumeration yielded actionable data even though exploitation remains pending.

next_experiments.title: Deploy customized HTTP exploit chains
next_experiments.description: Chain dirsearch findings with Burp Intruder to craft specialized payloads for identified admin panel vulnerabilities.

next_experiments.title: Optimize SSH brute force strategy
next_experiments.description: Integrate credential patterns derived from service banners with Hydra and limit rate to avoid lockouts while expanding password lists.

next_experiments.title: Persistence via web shell upload
next_experiments.description: Post-auth HTTP request to upload a minimal PHP web shell once valid creds from hydra are confirmed, then validate remote command execution.
